objects.docstring:
@poetry/agent - the WebMCP runtime. Register beside poetry's own
controllers:

  import { Application } from "@hotwired/stimulus"
  import { registerPoetryControllers } from "@poetry/controllers"
  import { registerPoetryAgent } from "@poetry/agent"
  const application = Application.start()
  registerPoetryControllers(application)
  registerPoetryAgent(application)

constants.name: controllers
constants.docstring: identifier -> controller class (the manifest introspects this).

constants.name: registerPoetryAgent
constants.docstring:
Registers the runtime's controllers, installs the versioned replace
stream action the AG-UI relay and the A2UI streams emit (when Turbo is
present), and the morph guards that keep an A2UI surface's local state
and an MCP App's frame through a streamed re-render.

objects.docstring:
The document.modelContext adapter - the ONE file that knows the WebMCP
surface's shape, so API churn (the spec changed twice over the summer of
2026 and again through the autumn, and the shipping browser trails it)
stays a one-file fix. Everything else in the runtime talks to this.

Spec surface (rev 6838130ef, 2026-10-27; config/upstream_watch.json pins
the specification repository there, and the upstream watch test holds
this line to the pin): document.modelContext with
registerTool(tool, {signal, exposedTo}), getTools({fromOrigins}) resolving
RegisteredTool dictionaries whose inputSchema is an object,
executeTool(tool, inputObject, {signal}) resolving the stringified
result, and the toolchange, toolactivated and toolcancel events on the
context (an EventTarget). ToolAnnotations carries readOnlyHint,
untrustedContentHint, consequentialHint and debugging.

Shipping-browser deltas this file absorbs (Chrome 151, measured
2026-09-01; spec issue #278 tracks them): getTools() reports inputSchema
as a serialized JSON string, and executeTool() parses ONLY a JSON-string
argument - an object rejects with UnknownError("Failed to parse input
arguments"), not a TypeError. Chrome 155 deprecates the string form, so
the object goes first and the string form is remembered only where a
browser taught it.

constants.name: modelContext
constants.docstring:
The live ModelContext, or null where the browser exposes none - callers
treat null as "do nothing", exactly like an edge bridge would.

constants.name: supported
constants.docstring: Whether this browser exposes a ModelContext.

constants.name: registerTool
constants.docstring:
Registers one tool; resolves when the browser accepted it, rejects on a
duplicate name, an empty name/description, or an invalid schema.

constants.name: getTools
constants.docstring:
The registered tools with inputSchema normalized to an object: parsed
when the browser serialized it, null when the text is not JSON.

constants.name: executeTool
constants.docstring:
Executes a tool with the spec's object arguments, falling back to the
JSON-string form the current Chrome build parses; when both shapes
reject, the first rejection surfaces.

constants.name: TOOL_NAME
constants.docstring: WebMCP tool-name grammar: 1-128 chars of ASCII alphanumerics, "_", "-", ".".

constants.name: validToolName
constants.docstring: Whether a name fits the WebMCP tool-name grammar.

constants.name: _resetArgumentShape
constants.docstring: Test seam: forget the argument shape the last browser taught us.

objects.docstring:
@poetry/agent/mcp_app - the page's half of the MCP Apps bridge: the
spec's JSON-RPC 2.0 over postMessage between a Poetry-rendered document
in a host's sandbox and the host. It initializes, takes the tool's input
and result, applies the fragments a result carries to the regions of the
page (the way Turbo Streams apply), calls the server's tools from marked
buttons and forms, posts a message to the chat, reports the page's size,
follows the host's theme, and maps the host's style variables onto
Poetry's tokens. No SDK, no imports: the same file runs from the app's
origin or inlined in the document.

Markup it reads:
  data-mcp-region="plans"          a region a fragment targets
  data-mcp-tool="choose_plan"      a button (or form) that calls a tool
  data-mcp-args='{"plan":"pro"}'   the button's arguments (a form sends its fields)
  data-mcp-message="..."           a button that posts a user message
  data-mcp-link="https://..."      a button that opens a link
  <html data-host-styles="structural|all|none">  the token mapping

Events it dispatches on document (detail carries the payload):
  poetry:mcp-app:connect, :input, :result, :fragments, :context, :error

methods.docstring:
Connects a bridge to the host when the page runs in a frame, and keeps
it at `window.poetryMcpApp`.

return.text: the bridge, or null outside a frame

objects.docstring:
Local state a morph must not reset inside an A2UI surface: the
selection a tab strip holds, a dialog's open state, a popup's expanded
state, and a control the user has edited (its value or checked state
differs from what the server last rendered). The server does not know
this state, so its frame would carry the defaults; canceling Turbo's
before-morph-attribute event keeps the page's own.

constants.name: installVersionedReplace
constants.docstring:
The versioned replace Turbo Stream action the AG-UI relay and the A2UI
surface streams emit: a streamed frame re-renders the SAME element from
a server stream, which inherits an out-of-order delivery race, so every
payload carries data-version and this action applies only strictly-newer
frames - older or duplicate frames are dropped silently. With
method="morph" the newer frame morphs the element through Turbo's own
replace action (idiomorph), so local state survives an update. Installed
on Turbo by registerPoetryAgent when the host has Turbo and no vreplace
of its own.

constants.name: preservesLocalState
constants.docstring:
Whether a morph must leave an attribute alone to keep an A2UI surface's
local state: an edited input's value or checked state, an open disclosure,
or a slot-specific attribute the runtime owns.

constants.name: preservesElement
constants.docstring:
Whether a morph must leave an element alone: the frame holder of an MCP
App (`data-mcp-app-host`) and everything inside it, which the host
controller owns. A stream morph would replace the holder outright (even
a `data-turbo-permanent` one) or strip its frame, and the app would
reload and handshake again.

constants.name: installMorphStateGuard
constants.docstring:
Installs the morph guards once per document, so a streamed re-render
morphs without clobbering local state or an app's frame.

objects.docstring:
A JSON-RPC error: what a handler throws to refuse, and what a failed host
request rejects with.

Exported from `@poetry/agent/mcp_app_host`.

The client side of an A2UI surface's checks: the server renders the
program (every checked component's rules, spelled as v1.0 spells them
whatever the surface speaks: `{"@path"}` bindings made absolute,
`{"@call", args}` calls, a literal `@` key doubled; the path each
checked control binds; the bound inputs by path with their kinds; and
the data model) and this controller evaluates it as the user types.

A button whose own checks fail is disabled from the start. What the
user sees of a failure waits for them: an input's message and invalid
state appear once its path has been edited, a button's reason once any
input has. Until then the server's rendering stands, including the
failures it rendered after a rejected action; one the browser cannot
judge (a rule on a function it does not know) stands until the server
judges it again. A morph keeps the element and this controller, so the
edited inputs are judged again once the morph is over.

The five validators and the three combinators are the checks
vocabulary; anything else passes here and is judged by the server,
which re-runs every rule on the action.

**Values**:
- `program` (Object): The check program the server compiled: the checks (each with the path its control binds), the bound inputs by path, and the data model.

methods.name: initialize
methods.docstring:
Starts with nothing touched: the paths the user has edited since the
surface mounted.

methods.name: programValueChanged
methods.docstring:
Evaluates every check at mount and again when a server render
changes the program.

methods.name: touch
methods.docstring: Marks the edited input's path touched and evaluates every check.

methods.name: morphed
methods.docstring:
Evaluates every check once a morph of the surface is over: the morph
left the slots and attributes as the server rendered them, and the
edited inputs keep their values. One pass per morph, however many
elements it touched.

methods.name: evaluate
methods.docstring: Runs every check in the program and applies its failures.

methods.name: failure
methods.docstring:
A rule's failure message, null when it passes, or undefined when it
cannot be decided here.

params.name: rule
params.text: the check rule with its condition and message

return.text: the failure message, null, or undefined

methods.name: apply
methods.docstring:
Reflects a check's verdict on the elements bound to a key. A button
disables while its checks fail. The message and the invalid state
follow the verdict only once the user has touched the input (any
input, for a button); before that, and for a server failure the
browser cannot judge, the server's rendering stands.

params.name: key
params.text: the bound key the elements carry

params.name: entry
params.text: the check entry: its kind (button or input) and the path its control binds

params.name: failures
params.text: the failure messages, empty when every decided rule passes

params.name: undecided
params.text: whether a rule could not be decided here

A value with its bindings read and its calls run, recursively; a

objects.docstring:
The AG-UI client-tool bridge: the relay appends one of these per tool
call the agent made to a FRONTEND tool - a component tool the page
declared - and this controller executes it through the registrar (the
same dispatch a WebMCP call takes, so it works in every browser,
modelContext or not), then POSTs the result to the continue URL. The
server folds the tool message into the transcript and answers with the
next run's streams, which Turbo renders. A tool declared to ask first
renders the host's approval prompt inside the element and waits: its
approve action runs the call, its deny action answers it as declined
without running it, and either answer hides the prompt. One element, one answer: the done flag makes a Turbo
re-render inert.

**Values**:
- `call` (Object): The pending tool call: its id, name and arguments.
- `url` (String): Where the tool result is posted.
- `done` (Boolean): Whether the call has already been answered (a restored snapshot must not answer twice).
- `confirm` (Boolean): Whether the call waits for the user's approve or deny before anything runs.

**Events**: `poetry:agui:client-tool-declined`, `poetry:agui:client-tool-executed`

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Runs the pending client tool once, unless it waits for the user.

methods.name: approve
methods.docstring: Runs the call the user approved.

methods.name: deny
methods.docstring: Answers the call as declined: the tool never runs, and the agent is told so.

objects.docstring:
The frame another server's MCP App renders in, and the host's half of
the bridge. The element carries the call (server, tool, input, result,
the app's resource) and where the sandbox page and the RPC endpoint
are; the controller reads the app's HTML through the endpoint, mounts
the sandbox proxy frame (on the apps origin, or as an opaque frame of
the page's own in the inline mode), answers `ui/initialize` with the
page's theme and tokens, delivers the input and the result, sends the
app's own requests to the endpoint, resizes to what the app reports,
moves the frame between the display modes (inline in the page,
fullscreen over it, pip in a corner), and tears the app down when the
element leaves.

What the page hears: `poetry:mcp-app-host:connect` (the app's info),
`poetry:mcp-app-host:message` (a message for the chat, `detail.params`),
`poetry:mcp-app-host:context` (a model-context update),
`poetry:mcp-app-host:display-mode` (a mode about to be entered, by the
app's request or the page's call: `detail.requested`, `detail.mode` the
controller is granting, which the handler may change, `inline` to
refuse), `poetry:mcp-app-host:authorize` (the endpoint wants the person
signed in to the server first: `detail.url`), and with `debug`,
`poetry:mcp-app-host:trace` for every message both ways. A link is
opened in a new tab after the person confirms it.

**Targets**: `frame`, `status`

**Values**:
- `server` (String): The server's id in the host's registry.
- `tool` (String): The tool the app belongs to.
- `resource` (String): The app's resource uri.
- `input` (String): The tool's input, as JSON.
- `result` (String): The tool's result (a CallToolResult), as JSON.
- `rpcUrl` (String): Where the app's own requests go: a POST taking { server, method, params }.
- `sandboxUrl` (String): The sandbox page's URL on the apps origin; absent in the inline mode.
- `sandboxOrigin` (String): The apps origin, the only origin the frame's messages are accepted from.
- `sandboxPage` (String): The sandbox page's HTML for the inline mode, written into an opaque frame of the page's own.
- `height` (Number, default: 160): The frame's height before the app reports its size, in pixels.
- `maxHeight` (Number, default: 4000): The most the frame grows to inline, in pixels.
- `displayModes` (Array, default: ["inline", "fullscreen", "pip"]): The display modes this page offers: inline, fullscreen and pip, in any subset.
- `pipWidth` (Number, default: 360): The pip panel's width, in pixels.
- `pipHeight` (Number, default: 480): The most the frame grows to in the pip panel, in pixels.
- `debug` (Boolean, default: false): Whether every message both ways is announced as a `poetry:mcp-app-host:trace` event, for a log.

objects.docstring:
The registrar: one controller on an opted-in component root
(`webmcp: "country"` on the helper call renders it beside the
component's own controllers) registers that instance's declared tools
with document.modelContext on connect and aborts them on disconnect.
Components gain zero runtime code - each tool dispatches to the
component's OWN controller action (the `executes` descriptor the Ruby
contract validated at class load), passing the tool's parameters
positionally in declared order.

Correctness rules the spec makes load-bearing:
- Re-registration is skipped while the payload is unchanged (the spec
  documents an unregister/quick-re-register race where in-flight args
  for the old tool can hit the new tool's schema).
- Never register under Turbo's cache preview.
- Duplicate names are rejected by the browser; we warn and skip.
- A per-document budget caps registrations (each tool costs the agent
  context; overlap confuses tool choice).
- Errors come back as descriptive result strings (granular exceptions
  are still open spec issues; a string lets the agent self-correct):
  a missing or unknown parameter, a value of the wrong type or outside
  the enum, a missing action, a throwing action.
- A result is the action's return value when it is JSON-serializable
  (the contract's actions return their resulting state, so an answer
  says what happened rather than "done"); the done marker covers
  actions that return nothing.
- Parameters map positionally onto the action in declared order; the
  execute callback's {signal} is not forwarded (the actions are
  synchronous UI operations).

**Values**:
- `name` (String): The instance name the tools register under (poetry.<name>.<tool>).
- `tools` (Array): The tool definitions this instance registers, as the component declared them.
- `budget` (Number, default: 20): The most tools one page registers; past it, further registrations are dropped with a console warning.

**Events**: `poetry:webmcp:executed`, `poetry:webmcp:registered`, `poetry:webmcp:unregistered`

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Registers this instance's tools and records it for the executor.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Forgets the instance and aborts its registrations.

methods.name: nameValueChanged
methods.docstring: Re-registers under the new name once connected.

methods.name: toolsValueChanged
methods.docstring: Re-registers the new tool list once connected.

methods.name: register
methods.docstring:
Registers every declared tool with the browser under the instance name,
within the page budget; skipped when unsupported or in a preview.

methods.name: execute
methods.docstring:
Runs one of this instance's tools by its registered or short name; an
unknown name resolves to an error message.

params.name: name
params.text: the registered or short tool name

return.text: the tool's result, or an error message for an unknown name

methods.name: unregister
methods.docstring: Aborts every registration of this instance and announces it.

objects.docstring:
The declarative-form companion: a form declared with poetry_webmcp_form
(toolname/tooldescription on the <form>) is registered by the BROWSER;
this controller only answers an agent-invoked submit with the outcome.
Chrome's SubmitEvent carries agentInvoked + respondWith(promise): we
submit the form ourselves (fetch, same method/action, Turbo-Stream
accepting) and respond with a short descriptive result instead of
navigating, so the agent learns whether the submission succeeded and
what the server said (validation errors included - it can self-correct).

The person's page then catches up with the answer (a beat after the
result is handed to the browser, so a navigation can never swallow
it): a GET answer is the page at that URL - a Turbo visit, or a plain
navigation without Turbo; a Turbo-Stream answer renders; a redirected
POST (redirect-after-create) visits where the redirect went. An HTML
re-render of a failed POST stays put - the agent already holds the
errors, and the person keeps their filled form.

Submits without agentInvoked (a person pressed Submit) pass through
untouched: the human path stays the human path.

The browser also tells the page when an agent runs a tool: toolactivated
fires on document.modelContext once the agent has filled a declarative
form (before its submit, or right before an autosubmit), and toolcancel
when the agent abandons the call because the person moved on to another
turn. For its own tool this controller marks the form
(`data-webmcp-agent="active"` until the cancel or the submit), dispatches
poetry:webmcp:tool-activated and poetry:webmcp:tool-cancelled on it, and
announces both through the shared live region - the agent's fill is a
change the person did not make. The browser's pseudo-classes carry the
visual; a browser without a model context hears nothing and loses nothing.

**Values**:
- `activatedMessage` (String, default: "Your agent filled this form. Review it, then submit."): What screen-reader users hear once an agent has filled this form.
- `cancelledMessage` (String, default: "Your agent stopped filling this form."): What they hear when the agent abandons the fill.

**Events**: `poetry:webmcp:form-submitted`, `poetry:webmcp:tool-activated`, `poetry:webmcp:tool-cancelled`

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring:
Listens for the form's submit, and for the browser's tool events when
it exposes a model context.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops listening, drops the agent marker and releases the live region.
